analysis.title: Commodity Monthly Review: Monthly Review – October 2026
key_insights: BCOM fell 0.4% in October to 141.2, bringing the year-to-date gain to 28.7%. Precious metals fell 9% and agriculture fell 5.6%, while energy rose 7.6%.

Energy was the best sector in October (+7.6%) and year to date (+95.0%). Brent rose 19.3% and WTI rose 15.2%, the two best performers in the complex, on Middle East supply risks tied to the US-Iran war.

Brent closed October in a volatile $100-118/bbl band, with six-month highs near $117 on 26-28 October. The December contract briefly approached $118 on 30 October, then the January contract pared gains to below $112 on news that Qatari mediators had returned to Tehran.
The WTI-Brent discount widened past $14/bbl. Hormuz flows ended the month near 54% of the pre-war baseline (~9.34 million b/d). ANZ raised its Brent year-end forecast to $105 from $95.
IEA, EIA and OPEC all trimmed 2026 demand forecasts, with OPEC cutting demand growth to 180 kb/d from 380 kb/d. SG says this failed to dent the conflict-driven floor under prices.

Dutch TTF rose about 43.8% in October and crossed €104/MWh on 30 October. EU storage was 75% full against a 90% five-year norm, and the winter's first net draw came around 20 October. JKM spot reached $34.63/MMBtu on 30 October.

US natural gas fell 9.3% on ample inventories and strong production. Henry Hub traded as low as $2.528/MMBtu on 20 October, when money managers held net shorts of 192,728 contracts, the most bearish positioning in six years. The 30 October EIA build was 80 Bcf against 75 Bcf expected.

Industrial metals fell 2.0%. Nickel fell 4.6% on higher Indonesian mining quotas (about 290Mt from about 260Mt) and oversupply. Reports of coordinated Indonesian HPAL production cuts caused a brief rally to $16,340/t on 21 October that faded by month-end.

Copper fell 2.1% but physical tightness persisted. Chilean Q3 mine output was 1.16Mt (-13% y/y, lowest in over 20 years), TCRC hit a new low of -67¢/lb, and the Yangshan premium reached a record of about $200/t. Managed money net length fell 22% to about 48k contracts.

Aluminium fell 2.9% on expectations of a larger 2027 surplus. PT Hua Chin Aluminum Indonesia applied to have 480ktpa approved for LME delivery, and Middle East smelters are restarting. LME and SHFE inventories fell 20% m/m and provided some support.
Zinc rose 0.4% on a concentrate shortage and import TCs of -160 to -200$/dmt. LME zinc stocks rose 30.1% in the month, with inventories jumping from 127kt to 168kt between 12 and 21 October.
Lead rose 1.2%. LME lead stocks fell about 46kt (-12.9%) to 311kt, while China's electric two-wheeler sales fell 4.8% y/y and sodium-ion batteries pose a medium-term substitution risk.

Precious metals fell 9%. Gold fell 6.9% to $3,874/oz, its weakest October since 2008, after a stronger-than-expected US CPI print lifted real yields. Gold dropped as much as 3.65% on 30 October during a technology-led equity sell-off.

Silver fell 18.6% and broke below $50/oz for the first time since October 2025, with a monthly low near $48.9/oz. Solar demand for silver is set to fall for a second year in 2026 as manufacturers reduce silver loadings, and the gold-to-silver ratio is rising.
The FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates at its 27-28 October meeting and left open a possible rate increase before year-end. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled fewer rate-setting meetings.

Central bank gold buying remained supportive. The PBOC added about 23 tonnes in September, its 23rd straight month of purchases, and Poland's reserves reached 673 tonnes. India's festive demand was hurt by a 3% IGST levy on bullion imports and limits on gold ETF subscriptions.

Grains fell 9.1% on larger US crop estimates and higher stocks. Corn fell 10.6% after the 9 October WASDE raised yield to 181.2bpa and ending stocks to 1.849bbu, and wheat fell 10.7%. Soybeans fell 5.8% and were resilient on high crush margins and export commitments.

Softs rose 1.4%. Sugar rose 4.0% on El Niño supply concerns, with the net speculative long above 220k lots, before a sharp long liquidation after Lula's win in Brazil's 25 October election weakened the real.

Arabica coffee fell 1.2% to 285 c/lb after reaching 318 c/lb on 20 October, retracing the rally on the Brazilian real's drop and favourable weather. Cocoa rose 1.6% on volatile El Niño supply fears and stronger Q3 grindings, offset by rising exchange stocks.

Livestock fell 4.9%. Lean hogs fell 15.2%, with front-month futures down from 77.5 to 58.9 USd/lb on demand destruction, weak Smithfield results and weak Chinese imports. Live cattle fell 0.8% on tight herd supply offset by softer boxed beef.

sector_views.rationale: Best-performing sector in October (+7.6%) and YTD (+95.0%), on Middle East supply risks and tight European gas storage.
Sector fell 9% in October on higher real yields, higher-for-longer rate expectations and weaker silver demand, partly offset by central bank buying.
Sector fell 2.0%. Physical tightness in copper and zinc contrasts with oversupply in nickel and a growing aluminium surplus.
Agriculture fell 5.6%, led by grains (-9.1%) and livestock (-4.9%), on larger crop estimates and weak pork demand. Softs rose 1.4%.

earnings_insights: BHP reported Q3 copper production down 19% y/y on adverse weather and lower ore grades, and kept full-year guidance.
Freeport-McMoRan cut Q4 copper sales guidance to about 397kt from 464kt on inventory accumulation at Indonesian smelters.

Smithfield Foods reported weaker-than-expected results and cut full-year revenue guidance, citing soft fresh pork demand. WH Group reported lower earnings and falling pork revenues despite higher sales volumes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Flat month overall, with energy gains offset by precious metals, agriculture and industrial metals declines.
Fiscal stress and energy-driven inflation pushed yields higher, which weighs on non-yielding assets such as gold.

macro_indicators.reading: 10-2 vote to hold rates at the 27-28 October meeting
macro_indicators.interpretation: Little guidance was given and a rate increase before year-end remains possible, which weighed on precious metals.

macro_indicators.reading: Stronger than expected in mid-October (figure not given)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Pushed real yields higher and pressured gold and silver.
Growth driven by manufacturing, technology and AI-related exports, with weak property and consumption limiting aluminium demand.

macro_indicators.reading: 80 Bcf vs 75 Bcf estimate, inventories 3,724 Bcf
macro_indicators.interpretation: Inventories are 38 Bcf above the five-year average, which is bearish for Henry Hub.
A 14-15 point deficit supports TTF and raises winter supply risk.
The bank cites fragile supply-demand balances since the conflict began.
A bearish revision that did not dent the conflict-driven price floor.
A large upside surprise that pushed corn sharply lower.

risk_factors: Escalation or resumption of US strikes on Iran, and attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, could drive further oil spikes.
Further Hormuz disruption would tighten LNG and oil supply.
Persistent EU gas storage deficit going into winter.
Higher-for-longer rates and a possible additional Fed hike weigh on precious metals.
A technology-led equity sell-off triggered liquidation across assets on 30 October.
A strong El Niño could disrupt sugar, cocoa and coffee supply.
Larger 2027 aluminium surplus and Indonesian nickel supply growth.
Crowded speculative positioning, as in sugar, leaves markets exposed to liquidation.
vol_and_positioning: Brent's second-month implied volatility hit its highest level since late July.
Henry Hub money managers held net shorts of 192,728 contracts on 20 October, the most bearish in six years.
Copper managed money net length fell 13.4k contracts (-22%) to about 48k.
Sugar net speculative long rose above 220k lots, one of the largest in recent years, before liquidation after the Brazilian election.
Copper cash-to-3M spread widened above $200/t, the highest since mid-August.
Zinc remains in backwardation and the cash-to-3M spread widened back above $100/t late in the month, while lead remains in contango at about -$30/t.
geopolitical: US-Iran war ongoing since March, with Hormuz flows at about 54% of the pre-war baseline and LNG transits below one third of pre-conflict levels.
Saudi East-West pipeline was halted on 5 October after a fresh attack, then recovered toward pre-conflict flows.
Houthi strikes hit King Khalid International and Abha airports, and the Houthis claimed an attack on Ras Tanura.
The White House reportedly asked the Pentagon for Iran strike options, and a US commander briefed Trump on resuming strikes after the midterms.
Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on 30 October.
The IRGC claimed a mine strike on a super tanker on 30 October.
EU ban on Russian long-term LNG contracts takes effect 1 January, and Novatek says it is ready.
Black Sea disruption continued, with drone strikes sinking a vessel in Bulgaria's EEZ and SovEcon cutting Russia's export forecast.
US 50% tariff on Canadian aluminium is reshaping trade flows.
Lula won Brazil's presidential runoff on 25 October, weakening the real.

tension_points.bull_case: Persistent Middle East supply risks, Hormuz flows at about 54% of baseline and attacks on Saudi infrastructure keep Brent in a $100-118 band, and ANZ raised its year-end forecast to $105.
tension_points.bear_case: IEA, EIA and OPEC all trimmed 2026 demand forecasts, and prices swing sharply on diplomatic headlines such as Qatari mediators returning to Tehran.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A diplomatic breakthrough that restores Hormuz and Saudi pipeline flows, or Brent falling below the $100 bottom of its band.

tension_points.bull_case: Reports of coordinated Indonesian HPAL output cuts briefly lifted nickel to $16,340/t on 21 October.
tension_points.bear_case: Indonesia raised mining quotas to about 290Mt, stocks remain elevated near 385kt and demand lags supply, so the market dismissed the cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Confirmed, sizeable coordinated production cuts that outweigh the higher Indonesian mining quotas.

tension_points.bull_case: El Niño risk in West Africa and Ecuador and expectations of a 2026/27 global deficit, with European grindings up 3.2% y/y.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising exchange inventories, strong Ecuadorian exports and the West African harvest ease nearby supply concerns.
